Reliance's telecom and broadband service Jio Platforms got listed in October 2026, achieving a market capitalisation of $137 billion, which made it the country's second-most valuable company after its parent.

Ambani's three children joined the board of Reliance in 2023. Son Akash heads Jio; daughter Isha oversees retail and financial services; and younger son Anant is in the energy business.

In 2026, Ambani announced plans for a $110 billion investment in AI infrastructure to be built across the country over the next seven years, the publication added.""

item.title: Sachin Tendulkar backs Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive
item.description: Sachin Tendulkar joins Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive as a strategic investor, backing its ambition to reach 100 million downloads amid growing competition in India's gaming industry.
item.content:encoded:
Metasports Interactive, the Hyderabad-based maker of cricket strategy game Hitwicket, has brought cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar on board as a strategic investor. He will also serve as the game’s brand ambassador.

Financial terms and valuation remain undisclosed. 

Existing backers include venture-capital firms Prime Venture Partners and Singapore’s Horizon Ventures, as well as cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle. 

This development is separate from the $20 million in user-acquisition funding it secured from London-based Metica in April. That earlier, non-dilutive facility was intended to fund marketing and international expansion without giving up equity.

Metasports has not specified how Tendulkar’s investment will be deployed. It aims to reach 100 million downloads within three years. The company claims Hitwicket has more than 20 million users across 120 countries, revenue doubled in the six months before the announcement, and players spend an average of 51 minutes daily on the game. 

According to the company, more than 97% of its revenue comes from in-app purchases, or optional items bought within the game. Its wider ambition is to build mobile sports gaming franchises beyond cricket.

Hitwicket is a multiplayer strategy title that puts tactical decisions ahead of reflexes. Players manage a virtual side and choose how to approach each ball. 

Tendulkar said it captures cricket’s strategic thinking, explaining that “Cricket has always involved reading the bowler, assessing the field and deciding the right approach for every ball.” He will also feature in the game and related content. 

Reddy said Tendulkar’s cricketing knowledge would help the team understand elite players’ decisions and refine gameplay.

India’s gaming market offers a substantial audience, although converting it into globally competitive businesses and original intellectual property remains a challenge. The Game Developer Association of India estimates that the country had 511 million players and $1.04 billion in video-game revenue in 2025. 

Recent funding deals demonstrate investor interest across genres. Bengaluru-based Spill Games raised $10.5 million in October, led by Elevation Capital, while social gaming platform Matiks raised $10 million led by General Catalyst. Cricket-focused LightFury Games also secured $11 million from investors including Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI and Times Internet.

Policy is shifting too. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, and its rules, effective from May 1, 2026, prohibit online money games while establishing a framework for e-sports and online social games, with user-safety and grievance-redressal requirements. Classification considers factors such as stakes, expected cash winnings and whether rewards can be converted outside a game.

item.title: Why best consumer brands are built on everyday habits, not one-time marketing campaign
item.description: For consumer brands, getting customers to try a product is only the first hurdle. The bigger challenge is getting them to return, particularly in a market where choices are abundant.
item.content:encoded:
Acquiring a customer may take a marketing campaign, but retaining one requires a product that becomes indispensable. At YourStory's Techsparks 2026, Sangeeth Krishna, founder, BRÜK and Nikhil Rajpal, founder of Qubo explained why design, reliability and an obsession with consumer behaviour are key to building lasting brands.

A security camera that lets parents check on their children, or an air purifier that quietly becomes part of a household routine. These products may serve very different needs, but they have one thing in common: their success depends on becoming part of consumers' everyday lives.

For consumer brands, getting customers to try a product is only the first hurdle. The bigger challenge is getting them to return, particularly in a market where choices are abundant, competing products are easily accessible and new brands are constantly emerging.

For Nikhil Rajpal, Co-founder of smart devices maker Qubo, the transition from a product being used regularly to becoming a habit is not necessarily reflected in usage metrics alone. "Real product-market fit happens once you've hit those hygiene usage metrics. If you speak to consumers, are they using superlatives? Are they saying things like, 'I can't live without this now'? That is when you realise you have probably hit product-market fit," he said.

The absence of a product, he believes, is often the best indicator of whether it has become a habit.

"A habit is not defined by usage metrics. A habit is defined by how much anxiety it causes you in its absence," said Rajpal, drawing a parallel with quick-commerce and food-delivery platforms that consumers increasingly depend on.

Designing for everyday use

Krishna of BRÜK saw that the opportunity in the drinkware market came from observing an emerging consumer trend. He noticed people matching their tumblers with their clothes and bags, much like they did with other lifestyle accessories.

He also saw a gap in the Indian market for premium drinkware with better finishing and build quality. The idea was to create a product that combined functionality with aesthetics, offering consumers an alternative in a category dominated by established players.

BRÜK’s product development focused on everyday convenience, particularly for people working in offices. "These are the small things we were very clear about. It has to be convenient for people to hold, carry and use," he said.

The broader principle is that a product must solve a real consumer problem before a brand can expect it to become a daily-use item.

Qubo's experience in the home-security category offers another example. Rajpal said consumers are generally reluctant to experiment with security products because the consequences of a failure could be significant.

"All you need to do is a good job. Provide a reliable service that consumers can depend on," he said. For Qubo, consistent performance and reliability are central to building trust, particularly in categories where consumers are unlikely to switch brands easily once that trust has been established.

Why retention cannot be a marketing function

With customer acquisition becoming increasingly expensive, brands often look at features, incentives and performance marketing to drive repeat usage. But Rajpal believes retention should primarily be a consequence of the product's usefulness.

"Marketing can only help you with acquisition, make users try for the first time. The product is responsible for making users come back and use it every day," he said. He cautioned against relying excessively on incentives such as streaks, points and cashback to bring customers back to a platform. Instead, brands should work backwards from consumer needs and build products that naturally encourage repeat usage.

Beyond the first purchase

For brands selling durable products such as tumblers, repeat purchases present a different challenge. Unlike consumables, customers are unlikely to replace their drinkware every few weeks or months.

Besides expanding its product range, BRÜK is also exploring adjacent product categories such as lunchboxes and protein shakers, building on its understanding of consumers' everyday routines. Adding to this, Krishna said founders need to constantly observe how consumers use products, including how they adapt them beyond their original purpose. He pointed to the accessories people add to their tumblers and the different bottles they carry to offices and gyms as examples of opportunities that can emerge from everyday observations.

"If you observe a person from morning to evening, you will get ideas. There is nothing magical about it. Just go around and observe," he said.

Premium pricing needs product value

Another challenge for emerging consumer brands is convincing customers to pay a premium when cheaper alternatives and established brands are already available.

Rajpal outlined two possible approaches: competing with established brands on the strength of a differentiated offering, or disrupting the market by providing comparable capabilities at a lower price through operational efficiencies.

As a brand gains consumer trust, it can gradually move away from an initial penetration-pricing strategy and improve margins.

"People are ready to pay if you have a quality product. The most important things are the build, the quality, the materials and the finish," said Krishna. For him, compromising on price simply to chase volumes is not necessarily the right strategy. A smaller but clearly defined customer base willing to pay for the product can be more valuable.

Ultimately, building a lasting consumer brand requires more than visibility or an aggressive acquisition strategy. In a crowded consumer market, that may be the strongest competitive advantage a brand can build.

item.title: Jewellery brand GIVA raises $100M from Multiples PE
item.description: Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.
item.content:encoded:
Multiples Alternate Asset Management along with its co-investors, has led the $100 million funding round in jewellery brand GIVA. 

Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.

The brand offers a diverse portfolio spanning 92.5 silver, gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery. It follows an omnichannel distribution model through its own retail stores, D2C website and leading third-party e-commerce and quick-commerce marketplaces. 

Currently, the brand retails through 400+ stores across India and Sri Lanka. The latest fundraise is the largest investment in India's new-age jewellery market, according to the company.

Ishendra Agarwal, founder & CEO, GIVA said, "Multiples’ backing is a strong endorsement of what we have built at GIVA since 2019, a high-growth, design-led fine jewellery brand that Indian consumers trust for everyday wear and gifting.”

“As we enter our next phase, we are focused on scaling our omnichannel presence, strengthening our manufacturing capabilities and elevating the fine jewellery experience for modern Indian consumers. With Multiples’ experience in helping new-age businesses scale, we have the right partner for this journey. This $100 Mn+ round, the largest investment in India’s new-age jewellery market, gives us the strength to move faster.”

The company also added that India's jewellery market is estimated to grow at around 6% CAGR to reach $124 billion by 2032. 

Multiples has also invested in brands such as Licious, ACKO, PVR and Arvind Fashions apart from in other sectors. Earlier this year, Multiples announced the close of a USD $430 million fund.

item.title: ideaForge takes flight as Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 124% to Rs 91 Cr
item.description: ideaForge achieved a Q2 FY27 financial turnaround with Rs 91.3 crore revenue and Rs 23.2 crore EBITDA, while advancing combat UAVs and securing Rs 151 crore RDI funding for heavy-lift logistics.
item.content:encoded:
Strong execution and technology innovation helped drive a sharp financial turnaround for Indian drone maker ideaForge in the second quarter FY27.

“Building on the steady start of the year in Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27 saw continued progress in order book execution, new product development, and preparations to capitalise on upcoming procurement opportunities,” said Ankit Mehta, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of ideaForge Technology.

A return to profitability

In Q2 FY27, revenue from operations reached Rs 91.3 crore, up 124% year-on-year (YoY) from Q2 FY26. For the half-year period H1 FY27, operating revenue surged 199% YoY to a record Rs 159.9 crore from Rs 53.5 crore in H1 FY26, driven by delivering over 50% of the opening order book.

Revenue streams were led by the defence vertical, which generated Rs 65.7 crore or 72% of Q2 FY27 operating revenue. The civil and enterprise segment contributed Rs 25.6 crore or 28% in Q2 FY27, driven by mapping projects, crowd safety monitoring, and Drone-as-a-Service software subscriptions, which offer cloud-based drone operations.

The company returned to profitability, reporting a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 6.5 crore in Q2 FY27, with a net margin of 7.1%. This compares with a loss of Rs 19.6 crore and a negative margin of 48.1% in Q2 FY26.

EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) stood at Rs 23.2 crore, with a margin of 25.4%, compared with a loss of Rs 8 crore and a negative margin of 19.6% in the year-ago quarter.

Q2 FY27 total expenses rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 90.1 crore. The largest cost centre in Q2 FY27 was material costs at Rs 48.1 crore, representing 53.4% of total expenses, followed by employee benefit expenses of Rs 16.6 crore (18.4%), other expenses of Rs 16.0 crore (17.8%), depreciation and amortisation of Rs 14.7 crore (16.3%), and finance costs of Rs 1.0 crore (1.1%).

Operational hurdles and expansion

“We have maintained our execution momentum despite persistent global supply chain constraints and a few delays in customer approvals for deliveries. While these challenges remain significant, we continue to closely monitor developments and take measures to minimise their impact on our operations and deliveries,” Mehta commented.

The firm secured Rs 151 crore in research debt funding from the Technology Development Board to develop YETI, a middle-mile logistics drone carrying 200 kg payloads over 200 km.

It completed field testing for the ZOLT hybrid tactical drone, offering 100 km range and 6 hours endurance with electronic warfare resilience to withstand signal jamming during intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions.

Additionally, equity capital raised via QIP enabled complete debt payoff.

However, hurdles remain with global supply bottlenecks, customer delivery acceptance sign-off delays, and a shrinking order book that stood at Rs 202.2 crore by Q2 FY27 end, down from Rs 350.8 crore in Q3 FY26 as execution outpaced new contract awards.

High working capital intensity also persists, with inventory at Rs 155 crore and trade receivables at Rs 161.1 crore. Nevertheless, an estimated Rs 20,000 crore Fast Track Procurement pipeline offers strong medium-term visibility.

item.title: Google launches Dreambeans app in India
item.description: Dreambeans is an experimental AI-powered app that creates personalised daily story collections.
item.content:encoded:
Google has launched Dreambeans, an experimental AI-powered app that creates personalised daily story collections, in India. Starting today, the app will be available in the country for users above 18 years.

Developed by Google Labs, Dreambeans turns users' digital activity into personalised and illustrated stories about their interests and life. The app was first rolled out in the United States in September.

“This could be everything from places to explore, new arts & crafts, or a reminder of upcoming local events. You can dive deeper into any story to learn more, bookmark for later, or easily share with others to spark inspiration," said Google in an official blogpost, adding that the app is designed to connect users with what matters without endless scrolling.

The app is available on both android and iOS, and can be accessed across 14 languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati, Kannada, Punjabi, Assamese, and Nepali.

Dreambeans creates curated stories using information from selected Google apps including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube. "Share your feedback to make your stories even better over time," said Google.

The app has a 'thumbs down' button to indicate that something is wrong with the content or is not relevant for the user. Users can also delete data anytime from the app via its settings. This deletes the data from the system as well.

item.title: PowerUp Money raises $10M to expand AI-led wealth management
item.description: The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.
item.content:encoded:
PowerUp Money, a wealthtech platform offering mutual fund advice and digital wealth management services, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, an early-stage investment firm.

Existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC also participated. 

The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.

PowerUp claims more than 1.5 million users track mutual fund portfolios worth over Rs 2.5 lakh crore on its platform. Its paid subscription service, Elite, provides research-backed mutual fund advice and is said to have crossed 1,00,000 paid members in less than a year.

The company has now introduced Elite Prime, an AI-enabled digital wealth advisory service designed to provide a more comprehensive financial planning experience. It assesses investors’ financial goals, risk appetite and existing holdings to suggest asset allocation, systematic investment plans (SIPs), lump-sum investments, portfolio rebalancing and withdrawal strategies. It can also identify gaps in portfolios and suggest diversification into assets such as gold, silver and international investments.

An AI wealth coach and personal assistant are intended to help users understand recommendations and make informed decisions. 

Founder and chief executive officer Prateek Jindal said, “AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally”, bringing personalised guidance within reach of investors who may not be able to afford traditional wealth management services.

PowerUp is also looking to expand Infinite, its managed wealth advisory offering. The service combines financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation and ongoing portfolio management with dedicated human advisers. 

According to the company, Infinite has accumulated nearly Rs 500 crore in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch, despite being available to a limited customer base. Making the service accessible to more investors is another priority for the new funding.

The expansion comes amid sustained growth in India’s mutual fund market. According to the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), industry AUM stood at Rs 82.64 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, up from Rs 15.8 lakh crore a decade earlier. Monthly SIP contributions also reached Rs 32,490 crore in September, reflecting the growing adoption of regular, long-term investing.

Investor interest has encouraged further funding across the wealthtech sector. Debt investment platform Wint Wealth raised Rs 250 crore in a Series B round in January, while wealth management firm Centricity secured Rs 280 crore in August. AI-focused advisory startup Novelty Wealth also announced a $1.4 million seed round in March.

However, growth brings its own challenges. Digital advice must remain suitable, transparent and compliant as platforms expand their customer base. SEBI issued an updated Master Circular for Investment Advisers in February, reinforcing the regulatory framework governing investment advice. 

The opportunity, as Flourish Ventures’ Asia head Ravi Kaushik noted, lies in helping investors manage increasingly complex financial lives.

item.title: OYO parent PRISM’s revenue rises 35% to Rs 2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27
item.description: PRISM's hotel segment bookings grew 30% year-on-year, while the vacation homes business recorded 28% growth in bookings.
item.content:encoded:
IPO-bound PRISM, parent entity of hospitality chain OYO, has posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 353 crore in the first quarter ended June, registering 17% growth from Rs 301 crore in the year-ago period.

The quarterly profit included a deferred-tax credit of approximately Rs 244 crore, according to the company's audited financials.

PRISM's revenue from operations increased 35% to Rs 2,814 crore in the first quarter of FY2026-27, compared with Rs 2,078 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, the audited financials showed.

The company's Gross Booking Value grew 30% to nearly Rs 9,600 crore in the same period.

Growth was broad-based across its hotels and vacation homes businesses.

PRISM's hotel segment bookings grew 30% year-on-year, while the vacation homes business recorded 28% growth in bookings.

Addressing shareholders at the company's Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) in early October, PRISM Founder Ritesh Agarwal said, "What is encouraging is that this momentum has continued into the first quarter of FY27. Our performance across hotels and vacation homes has demonstrated improving gross margins and higher operating earnings, even as we invest in expanding our brands and strengthening customer demand."

"We are continuing to grow our business while generating healthy operating earnings. We are seeing the benefits of the investments we have made over the past few years in technology, brands and distribution capabilities, while continuing to invest quite aggressively," he had said.

In his EGM address, Agarwal highlighted the importance of the company's geographically diversified business, with North America remaining a key market following the acquisition of G6 Hospitality. He said G6 alone contributed approximately Rs 14,000 crore in Gross Booking Value during FY26.

Other profitability indicators also strengthened in the June quarter: EBITDA rose 24% year-on-year to Rs 760 crore, while adjusted EBITDA, net of lease expenses, increased 35% to Rs 589 crore.

Its common technology platform is built centrally and replicated across markets, supporting pricing, distribution, reservations, customer service and property management. PRISM is also embedding AI in pricing and workflows; its Grace AI general manager supports operations at several hotels in Western markets. 

Separately, an October 26 addendum filed with SEBI cut the proposed IPO fresh issue to up to Rs 3,350 crore and earmarked Rs 2,512.5 crore for repayment or prepayment of borrowings through a subsidiary, while removing the proposed pre-IPO placement.

With inputs from PTI.

item.title: India's data centre capacity set for 5x surge by 2030: Crisil
item.description: The growth of data centres in India will also depend on factors like timely power supply, regulatory clearances and project execution capabilities.
item.content:encoded:
India's data centre industry is poised for an unprecedented investment boom, with installed capacity expected to increase five-fold to around 7.5 gigawatts (GW) by March 2030, attracting investments of more than Rs 3 lakh crore over the next four financial years, Crisil Ratings said in a report on Tuesday.

The expansion, fuelled by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), enterprise digitalisation and rising data consumption, is set to transform the country's digital infrastructure landscape.

However, the industry's ability to translate demand into sustainable returns will depend critically on timely power connectivity, regulatory clearances and disciplined project execution.

"Nearly half of the upcoming capacity is already committed under long-term contracts, limiting speculative development and reducing offtake risk," Crisil Ratings said. "Upfront tie-ups with hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and compute-intensive GenAI workloads, provide revenue certainty from the outset. This helps de-risk projects, even as the scale and speed of the planned build-out intensify execution requirements."

Strong demand from global hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and increasingly compute-intensive GenAI workloads, is also supporting investment decisions and reducing offtake uncertainty.

India's competitive cost structure is adding to its appeal as a data centre destination. Development costs are around 20 per cent lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets, reflecting relatively competitive land, construction and labour costs. Combined with lower power tariffs, this enables rental rates to be 30-35 per cent below those in peer markets. The availability of large campuses powered by renewable energy also strengthens India's proposition for hyperscalers seeking to meet sustainability commitments.

Says Anand Kulkarni, Director, Crisil Ratings, "India's structural cost advantages further strengthen its attractiveness as a data centre destination. Development costs are around one-fifth lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets owing to more competitive land, construction and labour costs.”

He further said, “Combined with lower power tariffs, this translates into rentals that are 30-35 per cent lower than in peer markets. The ability to develop large, renewable-powered campuses also aligns well with the sustainability goals of hyperscalers, reinforcing India's competitive positioning."

However, the scale of the planned expansion is placing considerable pressure on power infrastructure. Nearly three-fourths of the approximately 6 GW of upcoming capacity is expected to be concentrated in Visakhapatnam, Mumbai and Hyderabad, Crisil said.

By fiscal 2030, data centre capacity in these cities could be equivalent to around 80%, 60% and 20%, respectively, of their current peak electricity demand. This concentration makes timely grid connectivity and transmission capacity augmentation critical to avoiding commissioning delays and cost overruns.

item.title: India shines in Apple’s record September quarter
item.description: Apple achieved an all-time revenue record in India during CEO John Ternus’s debut quarter, as global revenue reached $114.48 billion despite unprecedented memory cost inflation.
item.content:encoded:
India emerged as a stellar growth market for Apple in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, registering an all-time company revenue record in the country.

“We also set September quarter revenue records in both developed and emerging markets, in addition to an all-time record in India,” Apple Chief Executive Officer John Ternus said.

The performance in India was propelled by a September quarter record for iPhone upgraders, with Worldpanel survey data ranking iPhone among the top-selling smartphone models in the country.

Mac sales also set an all-time revenue record in India, driven by demand for the new MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro.

Furthermore, Apple launched Apple Pay in India in this quarter in partnership with Axis Bank, extending digital payments to one of the world’s largest consumer markets.

“We are optimistic about the long-term future of our services business,” Apple Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh noted.

Global financials

Moving to global business, Apple generated quarterly total revenue from operations of $114.48 billion, an 11.72% YoY increase compared to $102.47 billion in Q4 FY25.

For the full fiscal year FY26, total revenue reached an all-time record of $478.83 billion, up 15.06% YoY from $416.16 billion, while full-year net profit reached $132.18 billion, up 18% YoY.

Quarterly revenue comprised two distinct streams: Products revenue of $82.90 billion (72.42% of total) and Services revenue of $31.57 billion (27.58% of total).

Across product categories, iPhone generated $57.58 billion (50.30% of total revenue), growing 17.46% YoY due to global upgrader records and demand for iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo.

Services achieved an all-time record of $31.57 billion, rising 9.82% YoY on record cloud, video, and payment revenues, with paid subscriptions topping 1.5 billion.

Mac revenue jumped 23.68% YoY to $10.79 billion due to strong MacBook Neo adoption and global market share gains. Conversely, Wearables, Home and Accessories fell 7.91% YoY to $8.30 billion against tough prior-year comparisons, while iPad revenue declined 10.40% YoY to $6.23 billion due to supply constraints.

Apple’s profit after tax rose 11.81% YoY to $30.71 billion, compared to $27.47 billion in Q4 FY25, assisted by a $0.05 per share tariff refund benefit.

On a full-year basis, EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation), which measures operational cash profit, reached $171.49 billion, delivering an EBITDA margin of 35.81% on $478.83 billion in revenue.

Expense drivers

Managing total operations required $59.66 billion in total cost of sales, up 10.22% YoY. Total operating expenses jumped 20.58% YoY to $19.19 billion.

Research and Development (R&D) represented the largest cost centre at $11.73 billion (61.13% of total operating expenses), surging 32.30% YoY from $8.87 billion as Apple accelerated investments in generative artificial intelligence (AI), such as Siri AI, and custom silicon.

Meanwhile, Apple’s active installed base stood over 2.5 billion devices, with $28.10 billion in quarterly operating cash flow, and $137 billion in cash reserves.

However, unprecedented memory cost inflation compressed profit margins, while supply limits on advanced nodes, cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing chips, restricted device availability.

“What we are seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. And as we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components,” Ternus explained.

Supply chain bottlenecks also hampered shipments.

“The Q4 constraints were primarily driven by the availability of the advanced nodes our SoCs are produced on. But as we have transitioned more of our lineup to the latest 2-nanometer technology nodes, our constraints on advanced nodes are easing,” Apple Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan said, detailing these operational challenges.

item.title: Customers withdraw $3.6B after largest theft in Binance's history
item.description: According to media reports, customers withdrew $3.6 billion of assets from Binance as it reopened on Sunday following the theft.
item.content:encoded:
Binance witnessed a massive increase in outflows, with customers withdrawing $3.6 billion from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange after the largest theft in its history, which has been linked to North Korea.

According to media reports, customers withdrew $3.6 billion of assets from Binance as it reopened on Sunday following the theft of $6.3 billion on Thursday.

The company had suspended all transactions following the incident.

"Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases at 06:00 UTC on November 1, 2026," the company posted on X on Sunday, three days after it froze assets in the wake of the theft.

"By 12:36 UTC, withdrawals had resumed for all 15 networks and assets in the initial phase. After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising as expected, while deposit volumes have remained substantial," it said.

According to Binance, customers deposited $1.01 billion and withdrew about $4.649 billion in assets. Most of those transactions occurred in the first few hours after trading was restored, it added.

The outflow of $3.64 billion represents 2.1% of $171 billion in total assets under its management, the company said on Sunday.

"Our team continues testing rigorously the remaining networks and assets. We know how important safe and reliable access to your funds is and will share details of the next phase as soon as we can. Rest assured that market conditions are stable,” Binance said in a post on X.

The company said that it would cover all losses that occurred during the hack and that it had worked with other cryptocurrency firms to freeze about USD 3 billion in stolen assets, according to a The New York Times report.

The paper said that the cybersecurity analysts and the FBI have attributed the theft to North Korea, which has targeted cryptocurrency companies for years, taking advantage of vulnerabilities in their infrastructure to steal assets.

"The hackers may have used artificial intelligence technology to accelerate their attack, according to the crypto analytics firm Chainalysis, which said that the attackers processed 'thousands of transactions in a short period'," the NYT report said.

Changpeng Zhao, a co-founder of Binance, said, "Trust isn’t earned by what you say in good times. It’s earned by what you do in hard times."

According to the NYT, he also warned customers to beware of online scammers making bogus offers of compensation.""
